threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus at the stop instead of walking two feet to the curb. The locals glide past, it's like a dance they mastered long ago.
Last night on the 59, a bloke serenaded the bus with an acoustic guitar. Didn’t catch his name, but he definitely knew all the classics.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really home when I saw a guy using his skateboard to carry groceries while chatting up a street musician outside the Rewe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do they stop trains for spontaneous dance parties on the U-Bahn. Last week, a DJ popped up at Kottbusser Tor, and everyone joined in!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their nonchalance during BART delays—while newbies are panicking, we're just checking the time and grabbing a taco.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo wait for the 5-Fulton while juggling. Just another Tuesday in the Tenderloin, I guess. Muni really brings out the characters.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but the real magic is in the narrow streets, where you can still find a grandmother selling pastries from her kitchen.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones staring at the metro map like it’s a treasure map, usually blocking the entrance and asking the locals for directions.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie by their confusion over the 'weird' bus routes that seem to loop back on themselves; only locals know that's just how it goes here.
Last night, a group of teens on the 133 were debating the best chicken shops, while a guy in the corner kept trying to film them. Classic Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I stepped outside and the waft of grilled kebabs mingled with the chatter of kids playing in the street. That’s Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a karaoke bar where locals earnestly belt out German punk hits at 2 AM, surrounded by friendly strangers. It's a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by the way they know to bypass the Civic Center when there's a dog on the tracks. Tourists just stand there confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, a bus driver did a whole karaoke set while we sat idling. Definitely a Muni moment—only in SF do you get a show with your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can haggle at local markets like Els Encants. Vendors here see that as an affront; it’s about respect, not just price.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to try the local ‘patates braves’—still preferring the bland chain fare close to their Airbnb.
